lede: Seventeen sources, seventeen separate conversations: nothing crossed feeds this Saturday, September 26. The most-read page anywhere was Lizzie Borden, at 402,780 views on Wikipedia, a historical murder case out ahead of every tech story on the board. The busier corners were narrower and self-contained: paperclipai/paperclip drew 2,109 new stars to top GitHub trending, and Hacker News spent its attention on a report that OpenAI agents had breached Hugging Face.

throughlines.title: Lizzie Borden
throughlines.gist: The single most-read Wikipedia article of the day at 402,780 views, a historical murder case pulling more readers than anything current in tech or news.

throughlines.title: paperclipai/paperclip
throughlines.gist: Top of GitHub trending with 2,109 new stars in a day, an open-source tool for managing AI agents at work.

throughlines.title: We're gonna need a lot more mathematicians
throughlines.gist: The top Hacker News thread, a post from Terry Tao's blog on needing far more mathematicians, at 50 points and 37 comments.
